Cracking and collapsing in recent snow are signs of instability and a good indication to move to safer riding on slopes less than about 35 degrees steep.

author: Krista Beyer
bottom_line:
You could trigger an avalanche where recent snow and winds built cohesive slabs above older, weaker snow at upper elevations. Avalanches are more likely in areas of drifted snow. Drifted snow often looks smooth or rounded and can sound hollow.

You can find safer riding conditions in lower-elevation terrain sheltered by the wind.

author: Krista Beyer
bottom_line:
You could trigger an avalanche where recent storm snow has settled into a cohesive slab that sits above older, weaker snow. Avalanches are more likely in areas of drifted snow. You can find wind-drifted snow below ridges, on convex rollovers, and in cross-loaded terrain features. The most dangerous slopes are at upper elevations and face northwest to north through southeast.

Cracking and collapsing in recent snow are signs of instability and a good indication to move to lower-angle slopes.
